note: Living content ledger for NRITOUSA.com. THIS FILE IS THE HAND-MAINTAINED PART — the backlog of content work we know about. Everything else in the rendered ledger (link health, meta stats, verified-number status, the Fast Answer coverage gap) is regenerated from the audit scripts each run, so it can never drift from reality. Regenerate with `npm run ledger` (needs a prior `next build`). Add an item when an audit surfaces work we are not doing today; move it to status:done with a `resolved` date when it ships. Do not delete resolved items — the log is the record of what changed and when.

items.title: 79 high-intent pages still lack the verified-numbers treatment
items.detail: audit:intent-numbers scores every route that answers a number question against six affordances: a Fast Answer block, a numeric estimate, a last-verified stamp, an official-source link, FAQ schema, and an Article dateModified. 79 High-priority pages are missing at least one. The H-1B lottery cluster is the weakest — most of those pages have FAQ schema and nothing else, so they make numeric claims with no stamp and no citation.
items.nextStep: Work the High tier in cluster order (h1b-lottery first, then education, then green-card/[slug]), adding FastAnswerSnapshot + OfficialSourceNote and moving any inline figures into the cluster data file.

items.title: 21 verified-number stamps are now past the 45-day threshold
items.detail: 21 of 29 tracked values carry lastVerified 2026-07-04, which crossed STALE_DAYS (45) on 2026-08-19 — audit:monthly-numbers now flags all 21. The values themselves were confirmed correct on 2026-08-18 against USCIS Form G-1055 (Ed. 05/29/26) and DOL FLAG, so this is a stamp-refresh task, not a data-correction task. Do NOT bump the dates without re-checking: a date is not evidence, which is the whole reason the drift check exists.
items.nextStep: Re-verify the travel.state.gov NVC fees and the passport/VFS ranges by hand (both hosts block automated fetches), then run `npm run audit:monthly-numbers:baseline` to move the stamps and the baseline together.

items.title: PWD planning band (4–8 months) now runs ahead of DOL's own queue
items.detail: permProcessingData.ts plans prevailing-wage determinations at 4–8 months. DOL FLAG's receipt months imply faster: OEWS PERM cases filed April 2026 were being processed as of 30 June (~2–3 months), non-OEWS March 2026 (~3–4). The stored receipt months match DOL exactly, so the underlying data is right — it is the derived band whose floor sits above observed reality. Defensible as a buffer while DOL's PWD table is itself seven weeks stale, but it is the one figure where we tell readers to expect worse than they will likely get.
items.nextStep: Re-check flag.dol.gov/processingtimes when DOL refreshes the PWD table; if the receipt months hold, drop pwdPlanningMonthsLow to 3.

items.title: 223 titles exceed the SERP display limit
items.detail: Median indexable title is 64 characters; 223 exceed 60 and 63 exceed 80, topping out at 95. Google rewrites rather than penalises, so this is not an error — but the tail is where the keyword differentiators sit, and on a 95-character title the tail is always cut. Worst offenders are the long descriptive titles on /articles/real-estate-first-investment-immigrants, /can-h1b-parents-open-trump-account-for-child and /india-business-visa-from-usa.
items.nextStep: Trim to ~57 chars before the ' | NRI to USA' template, front-loading the keyword. Batch by cluster so sibling titles stay parallel.

items.title: 152 meta descriptions exceed 160 characters
items.detail: Median is 154 characters, but 152 pages exceed 160 and 34 exceed 200, with a 310-character outlier on /india-investments/should-nris-keep-investments-in-india. Long descriptions are simply truncated in the SERP; the risk is that the sentence carrying the click argument is the one cut.
items.nextStep: Rewrite the 34 pages over 200 characters first — below that the loss is marginal.

items.title: 30 outbound citations can only ever be verified by hand
items.detail: uscis.gov, travel.state.gov, vfsglobal.com, finra.org, congress.gov, migrationpolicy.org and a few others answer 403 to any automated request. link-health.js classifies these as 'unverifiable' rather than dead so they do not generate false alarms — but it also means link rot on exactly the hosts we cite most would go undetected. USCIS silently retired five paths before the 2026-08-18 audit caught them, and those were only visible because www.uscis.gov happens to answer 404 rather than 403.
items.nextStep: Spot-check the travel.state.gov and vfsglobal citations by hand each time the monthly numbers are reconciled.

items.title: 29 citations still resolve, but only through a redirect
items.detail: Nothing here is broken today — each one 301s to live content — but a redirect is a warning shot, and several are agency reorganisations that will eventually be dropped. The substantive ones: USDA renamed FNS to FNA (fns.usda.gov → fna.usda.gov, 2 citations); benefits.gov now hands off to usa.gov's benefit finder; acf.hhs.gov moved to acf.gov; the IRS ITIN page moved under /tin/itin/ and its early-distributions page is now 'exceptions-to-tax-on-early-distributions'; California's notary authentication page became request-apostille. The high-traffic ones are cosmetic (uscis.gov/forms → /forms/all-forms on 12 pages, incometax.gov.in → its portal path on 24).
items.nextStep: Update the agency-rename cases (USDA, ACF, benefits.gov) on the next government-benefits pass; leave the cosmetic ones. Re-check with `npm run ledger:links`.

items.title: Duration-of-status rule: re-verify after the Sept 9 hearing and the Sept 15 effective date
items.detail: DHS final rule (pub. 2026-07-17) ends D/S and cuts the F-1 grace period from 60 to 30 days from 2026-09-15. Challenged 2026-08-18 in D. Mass. (Presidents Alliance v. DHS, 1:26-cv-13799); govt response due 08-31, injunction hearing 09-09. The student cluster currently models 60 days because students already admitted for D/S keep it until they travel. If the rule survives, optRules.gracePeriodDays handling and the OPT calculator grace milestones need revisiting.

items.title: OPT-denial grace period — RESOLVED against the USCIS Policy Manual
items.detail: Resolved 2026-08-20. USCIS Policy Manual Vol.2 Pt.F Ch.5: an initial post-completion OPT denial leaves F-1 status expiring 60 days from the program end date or the denial date, WHICHEVER IS LATER — except where the denial was for failure to maintain status, in which case immediate departure is expected. A STEM extension denied after the OPT EAD expired ends status 60 days from the denial date. All three branches are now encoded in optDenialRules and rendered on the OPT calculator, with tests.

items.title: Proclamation 10973 lapses 2026-09-20 unless extended — recheck the $100K H-1B fee framing
items.detail: Proclamation 10973 was written as a 12-month measure scheduled to expire 2026-09-20 unless extended, renewed or superseded. Separately, the implementing policy was vacated 2026-06-08 and the First Circuit declined to reinstate it 2026-07-24, so it is not being collected. Do NOT simplify this to 'the fee expires on Sept 20' — expiry and vacatur are independent, and either could change first.
items.nextStep: Recheck on/after 2026-09-21; update h1bProclamationFee.statusLine to reflect whichever ended it — expiry and vacatur are independent tracks, do not collapse them into 'the fee expired'

items.title: Public charge citation pointed into USCIS's archive
items.detail: governmentBenefitsData.ts cited the USCIS Public Charge Resources page, which now 301s into /archive/. That matters more than a normal redirect because this cluster tracks a public charge rule taking effect 2026-09-18 — a reader following an archived link for a rule about to change is being pointed at superseded guidance. Policy Manual Part G was already cited alongside it, so the slot now points at the USCIS rescission notice, which independently confirms the Sept 18, 2026 date the cluster carries.
